evidence: Absence: no 'rollback', 'revert', or 'back-out' language anywhere in the plan.

findings.finding: The plan acknowledges the string-literal breakage risk and enumerates all affected call sites, but provides no explicit rollback or back-out procedure. T4 requires an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing as the remedy — acknowledgement alone is insufficient. If the string-literal patch is inadvertently omitted or mis-applied, there is no documented recovery step (e.g. 'revert the branch', 'run git revert <sha>', or 'apply in expand-contract order').
findings.location: ## Approach / ## Testing / ## Acceptance Criteria — no rollback section exists

findings.finding: The affected-file inventory for `_anthropic_cache_settings` was produced by `grep` alone, not by `find_referencing_symbols` followed by a separate string-literal grep. The plan's own text states this explicitly. `grep`-only derivation is the known failure mode documented in `docs/code-navigation.md` for this exact symbol: it misses structural references (false positives from comments, wrong semantic scope) and — in the opposite direction — is the only tool that CAN catch string-named sites like `monkeypatch.setattr`. Neither tool is a superset of the other; the safe derivation sequence requires both.

scenarios: If a future rename plan follows the same grep-only method on a symbol with comment mentions, grep will surface false-positive 'sites' that do not need patching — wasting effort or causing incorrect edits.
If `find_referencing_symbols` is not run, any new structural call site added between the grep run and execution (e.g., a newly imported alias) will be silently omitted from the patch scope.
